# A worked example

## Strict convexity

::: {#def-strict-convexity}
A function $f$ on an interval is strictly convex if for any distinct $x$ and $y$ in the interval and any $\lambda \in (0,1)$,
$$
f(\lambda x + (1-\lambda)y) < \lambda f(x) + (1-\lambda)f(y).
$$
:::

::: {#thm-quadratic}
The function $f(x)=x^2$ is strictly convex on $\mathbb{R}$.
:::

::: {.proof}
For $x \ne y$ and $\lambda \in (0,1)$,
$$
\lambda x^2 + (1-\lambda)y^2 - (\lambda x + (1-\lambda)y)^2
= \lambda(1-\lambda)(x-y)^2 > 0.
$$
This is the inequality in @def-strict-convexity.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Example"}
By @thm-quadratic, squaring the average of two distinct numbers gives less than the average of their squares. For $1$ and $3$, the two quantities are $4$ and $5$.
:::
